::: {.who}
[Damian L. Gallegos Espinoza]{.name}

[Ph.D. Student in Computer Science · The University of Texas at El Paso]{.role}

I study how neural networks handle uncertainty: how confident they are, and how
wrong they're likely to be. Most of my work is on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs).

::: {#research .panel role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="t-research"}
[Research]{.panel-title}

I'm a Ph.D. student in Computer Science at UTEP. I started out in Materials
Engineering at UACJ, moved into data science for my M.S., and now work on the
part of machine learning I find most interesting: knowing what a model doesn't know.
I focus on three questions about KANs:

::: {.topics}
::: {.topic}
[01]{.num}

**How do we train them well?** Adaptive optimizer sequencing that runs L-BFGS
first, tested with ablations against baselines
([MICAI 2026, code on GitHub](https://github.com/dlgallegose/Adaptive-Optimizer-Sequencing-for-Kolmogorov-Arnold-Networks)).
:::

::: {.topic}
[02]{.num}

**Can we read them?** Extracting symbolic formulas from trained KANs in Julia,
so a model can be read as an equation.
:::

::: {.topic}
[03]{.num}

**When are they wrong?** Hessian-based estimates of a model's confidence and
expected error.
:::
:::
:::
